newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks drop on economic slowdown fears.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks drop on economic slowdown fears.

text.p: Manila stocks took another dive on Monday on lingering fears the Philippines is heading the way of Thailand's economic problems.
"Comparisons made between the Philippines and Thailand continue to hound the local market," said Ardee Garcia, analyst at Diversified Securities.
The 30-share composite index hovered near its support of 2,500 after it ended at 2,509.36, down 66.77 points.
Traders said soaring domestic rates, with the Central Bank aggressively defending the peso to ward off speculation on the market added to the market woes.
Investors shrugged off reports U.S. debt rating agency Moody's Investors Service upgraded the long term foreign currency deposit rate of the Philippines, they said.
Trading was subdued, with some 1.2 billion pesos worth of shares changing hands, as worries on whether or not the U.S. Fed will increase its rates on Tuesday kept foreign funds on the sidelines.

Losers overwhelmed gainers 120 to 16. "Until we can get out from the shadow of Thailand and until we know the successor of President Fidel Ramos next year, the market will continue treading on dangerous ground," Garcia said.
